name: Minil Songa
instructions: 1. Soak the sticky rice (Minil) in water for a few hours to soften it.
2. Clean the bamboo tube thoroughly and ensure it is green and fresh.
3. Pack the soaked rice into the bamboo tube, adding just enough water to allow the rice to steam properly.
4. Seal the opening of the bamboo tube securely using a wad of banana leaves.
5. Place the bamboo tube directly over an open fire or hot coals.
6. Rotate the tube occasionally to ensure even cooking until the bamboo is charred and the rice inside becomes soft and fragrant.
7. Break open the bamboo to serve the steamed sticky rice warm.
description: Minil Songa is a quintessential Garo culinary specialty from Meghalaya. The use of bamboo imparts a distinct earthy aroma to the sticky rice, a staple in tribal households. Traditionally prepared during community gatherings or family meals, it highlights the indigenous technique of cooking using natural vessels found in the forest.
